title: Manufacturing of a Nafion-coated, Reduced Graphene Oxide/Polyaniline Chemiresistive Sensor to Monitor pH in Real-time During Microbial Fermentation
protocol: Add 3 g of graphite into 69 mL of concentrated H2SO4 and stir the solution until the graphite has completely dispersed.
Add 1.5 g of sodium nitrite and leave it for 1 h while stirring.
Place the container in an ice bath.
Add 9 g of potassium permanganate into the dispersion and remove the container from the ice bath.
Allow the solution to warm up to room temperature.
Add 138 mL of distilled water dropwise.
Continue to add 420 mL of distilled water.
Maintain the temperature at 90 °C for 15 min using a hotplate.
Add 7.5 mL of 30% hydrogen peroxide to the dispersion.
Collect the product by centrifugation at 10,000 x g for 20 min and discard the supernatant solution.
Wash the pellet 4x with warm double-distilled water.
Wash the pellet 2x with a 10% HCl (v/v) solution.
Finally, wash it 2x with ethanol.
Dry it at 50 °C in the oven.
Disperse 10 mg of graphite oxide in 10 mL of water and then sonicate it in an ultrasonic bath for 6 h.
Remove the unexfoliated graphite oxide flakes by centrifugation for 30 min at 2,700 x g.
Discard the solid particles after centrifugation and use the supernatant for further experiments.
Add 2 μL of the GO working solution on top of an exposed interdigitated gold electrode.
Dry the electrode at room temperature for 12 hours.
Insert the electrode into a PDMS electrode holder (bottom piece).
Place the other part of the electrode holder, which serves as a solution reservoir, on top of the electrode.
Clip together the two parts of the holder using paper clips.
Ensure that the PDMS holder does not cover the GO-deposited electrode part.
Pipette 300 μL of 0.2 M phosphate buffer (pH 7) into the reservoir.
Place the reference and counter electrodes in the solution close to the surface of the GO film.
Connect the electrodes with a potentiostat connected to a computer for data acquisition.
Use cyclic voltammetry: select 0 to -1.2 V as potential range, and 50 mV/s as scan rate.
Cycle the voltage over the electrode between 0 to -1.2 V ten times.
Remove the electrode from the holder after the experiment.
Wash the electrode repeatedly with double-distilled water.
Dry the electrode in an oven at 101 °C for 12 hours.
When the electrode is dry, remove it from the oven and allow it to cool down to room temperature.
Measure the conductivity of the electrode with a multimeter.
Prepare 10 mM aniline monomer for polyaniline functionalization.
Dissolve 5 µL of 10 mM aniline in 5 mL of 1 M H2SO4.
Add 300 µL of aniline monomer to the solution reservoir.
Place the ERGO-deposited electrode into the electrode holder as described for GO reduction.
Use cyclic voltammetry with a potential range of 0 to 0.9 V and a scan rate of 50 mV/s for polyaniline functionalization.
Cycle the voltage over the electrode between 0 to 0.9 V for 50 cycles.
Remove the electrode from the solution after polyaniline deposition.
Wash the electrode repeatedly with double-distilled water.
Dry the electrode at 80 °C in the oven for 12 h.
Allow the electrode to cool down to room temperature before measuring its conductivity with a multimeter.
Prepare a pH 5 buffer solution by adding 0.2 M NaOH to Britton-Robinson buffer until pH 5.
Keep the electrode in the pH 5 buffer solution for 24 h.
Mix 0.04 mol of phosphoric acid, 0.04 mol of acetic acid, and 0.04 mol of boric acid in 0.8 L of ultrapure water.
Add 0.2 M sodium hydroxide dropwise to the buffer solution until the desired pH is reached.
Add ultrapure water until the final volume is 1 L.
Condition the ERGO-PA electrode in a pH 5 buffer solution.
Measure the resistance of the electrode in solutions with different pH values from pH 4 to pH 9.
Dip the electrode directly into each buffer solution for measurement.
Connect the electrode to the computer-controlled potentiostat for data acquisition.
Change the pH by titrating with 0.2 M NaOH as needed.
Choose chronopotentiometry or amperometry i-t curve from the list of techniques and apply a 100 mV potential difference to the electrode.
Use Ohm's law (resistance equals voltage divided by current) to calculate resistance values.
Dry the electrode at room temperature for 12 h after measurements.
Add 5 µL of 5 wt% Nafion on top of the ERGO-PA electrode.
Dry the Nafion-coated electrode at room temperature for 12 h.
Add 9.3 g of M17 powder into 250 mL of ultrapure water.
Slowly agitate the solution until the powder dissolves completely.
Autoclave the solution at 121 °C for 15 min.
Take a 250-mL sterilized flask with a magnetic stirrer bar and add 50 mL of the sterilized M17 medium to the flask.
Add 8 mL of autoclaved 1 M glucose solution to the flask.
Inoculate the solution with 10 µL of an L. lactis culture, previously grown in the same culture medium.
Place the flask with the inoculated culture medium for 18 h on a magnetic stirrer plate in an incubation oven at 30 °C while stirring and monitor the pH.
Place the ERGO-PA-NA electrode into the L. lactis culture and close it with a cotton plug.
Place the set-up into the thermostat at 30 °C to grow L. lactis.
Apply 100 mV to the electrode and measure the current against time.
Take 0.5-mL samples at different time points.
Measure the optical density at 600 nm off-line.
Measure the pH with a conventional glass electrode.
Continue measurements until the optical density of the culture becomes constant.
